key_insight: SCOPE leverages unlabeled background regions in base-training 3D scenes to enrich class prototypes, enabling robust incremental few‑shot 3D segmentation that reduces forgetting and produces more discriminative novel-class representations.
problem_solved: Addresses incremental few‑shot 3D segmentation where new classes must be learned from very few annotations without catastrophic forgetting; existing methods struggle under sparse supervision and ignore the cue that novel classes often appear as unlabeled background during base training.
method: Scene‑contextualized prototype enrichment: mine background regions in base scenes to generate pseudo‑examples and augment few‑shot prototypes for novel classes.
Prototype refinement and regularization: refine enriched prototypes in feature space (e.g., contrastive or separation objectives) to improve discrimination and mitigate catastrophic forgetting.
Plug‑and‑play integration: a lightweight module that attaches to standard 3D segmentation backbones, enabling incremental updates from few annotations without full retraining.
impact: Makes 3D perception systems practical for real‑world deployments (robotics, autonomous vehicles, AR) by enabling them to learn new object classes from few labels while retaining previously learned categories. Reduces annotation costs and frequent full re‑training.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: base-training scene → background mining → prototype enrichment → incremental update to segmentation backbone
